'''Matthias Aschenbrenner'''  (born 1972 in [[Bad Kötzting]]) is a German-American mathematician. He is a [[Professor of Mathematics|professor of mathematics]] and director of the logic group at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref name="ViennaWelcome">{{cite web|url=https://mathematik.univie.ac.at/en/newsevents/full-news-display/news/welcome-matthias-aschenbrenner/?no_cache=1&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&cHash=33d8a72fc8a85f4c75895f7e7c9fba6f|date=July 15, 2020|title=Welcome, Matthias Aschenbrenner!|website=University of Vienna|access-date=August 6, 2020|archive-date=August 8, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808000529/https://mathematik.univie.ac.at/en/newsevents/full-news-display/news/welcome-matthias-aschenbrenner/?no_cache=1&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&cHash=33d8a72fc8a85f4c75895f7e7c9fba6f|url-status=dead}}</ref> His research interests include [[differential algebra]] and [[model theory]].<ref>[https://www.math.ucla.edu/~matthias/ Matthias Aschenbrenner]</ref>

==Career==
Aschenbrenner earned his "Vordiplom" at the [[University of Passau]] in 1996.<ref name=ViennaCV>{{cite web|url=https://medienportal.univie.ac.at/uniview/professuren/cv/artikel/univ-prof-matthias-aschenbrenner-phd/|date=July 2020|title=Univ.-Prof. Matthias Aschenbrenner, PhD|website=University of Vienna|access-date=August 6, 2020}}</ref> In 2001, he received his Ph.D. from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], where he was a student of [[Lou van den Dries]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=59951|title=Matthias Aschenbrenner}}</ref> For his dissertation, he was awarded the 2001 Sacks Prize by the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/sacks-prize-recipients/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722150030/https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/sacks-prize-recipients/ |archive-date=July 22, 2019 |url-status=live|title=Sacks Prize Recipients|author=<!--Not stated-->|publisher=[[Association for Symbolic Logic]]|access-date=January 27, 2020}}</ref> After a visiting position at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], Aschenbrenner joined the faculty at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] in 2003, moving to the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 2007.<ref name=ViennaCV/> In 2012, Aschenbrenner became a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=2014-12-20 |archive-date=2018-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was jointly awarded the 2018 [[Karp Prize]] with [[Lou van den Dries]] and [[Joris van der Hoeven]] "for their work in model theory, especially on asymptotic differential algebra and the model theory of transseries".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aslonline.org/files/newsletters/pdfs/April2018newsletter.pdf|title=ASL Newsletter|author=<!--Not stated-->|date=April 2018|publisher=[[Association for Symbolic Logic]]|access-date=July 20, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722150030/https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/ |archive-date=July 22, 2019 |url-status=live|title=Karp Prize Recipients|author=<!--Not stated-->|publisher=[[Association for Symbolic Logic]]|access-date=January 27, 2020}}</ref> In 2018, Aschenbrenner was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|author=<!--Not stated-->|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=June 21, 2019}}</ref> Aschenbrenner moved to the [[University of Vienna]] in 2020, where he is also director of the logic group.<ref name=ViennaWelcome/><ref name=ViennaCV/>
